## Result

- Skill: design-review
- Review status: changes-requested
- Package members: release — docs/design/release/release.md; system — docs/design/system/system.md; design — docs/design/design/design.md; published-skill-first-release-amendment — specs/published-skill-first-repository-simplification.md. Exact subjects and contextual inspection basis are stored with this record.
- Upstream review ID: proposal-review-r2, approved and current.
- Review ID and round: design-review-r1, round 1.
- Material findings: design-r1-f1; design-r1-f2.
- Correction targets: release; design authoring.
- Recording status: recorded through targeted batch upon successful save.
- Open blockers: no missing authority or unassessable package; two required corrections prevent approval.
- Immediate next stage: return to owning design author through Route; no Delivery reliance yet.
- Claim limitations: Design assessment only; no implementation, source deletion, runtime conformance, release, publication, Verify or PR readiness.

## Complete-package assessment

The four-member package is direction-aligned and feasible. Release has a coherent operational responsibility distinct from generation, installation and engineering assessments. The adoption boundary remains prospective through reviewed implementation and successful Verify. System references its owner and composition; Design extends DES-SR-21 only for this source group. The legacy amendment is new-profile-only: R7/R8 ownership transfers at adoption, with original IDs, boundary/examples and unselected populations preserved. It does not require rebuilding the retained feature boundary record. The inline Design example remains unchanged and coherent; no separate changed example is selected.

The complete six selected originals were inspected: both specifications, both test specifications and both ADRs. The model preserves version/dist-tag decisions, candidate identity, preparation side-effect limits, profile authority, generated/human/history distinction, closed marker/literal/timing shapes, pending evidence, preflight/full verification separation, local/CI composition, public evidence and rerunnable closeout, uncertain-write recovery, emergency record completeness, non-deferrable obligations, security and explicit freshness. The two findings below identify precise remaining meaning-transfer gaps, rather than a demand to copy the sources verbatim.

The substantive unnumbered content and ADR alternatives are addressed, including ad hoc versus repeated ceremony, version-scoped evidence, typed profiles, preflight-only/templates-only limitations and timing-before-optimization rationale. Completed authoring/milestone instructions and retired lifecycle writers are explicitly dispositioned. Historical claims are not retargeted. The map's six-file list and exact mixed-architecture paragraph/section boundaries are inspectable; nine removed and three retained paragraphs of Release and adapter evidence preserve the distribution/history remainder. No whole-directory, general diagram, schema, fixture, baseline, historical record or test deletion is selected.

Necessary consumer categories include current release guidance, System, scoped retention/source amendment, grandfathering manifest, actual historical literal baseline, scripts/CI/selectors, package inputs/current metadata and FU-013's remainder. Delivery must confirm actual readers and current metadata impact rather than assume source-only status. That allocation remains appropriately downstream. The presence of scripts and representations does not establish runtime conformance; no such claim is needed to assess this source transfer. Existing operational safeguards, local/CI and external observation boundaries remain intended constraints.

All eight scenario dimensions have requirement-grounded outcomes, with meaningful composed hazards: local/package success versus wrong hosted identity, delayed public observation after immutable write, and deletion with a live reader. Missing data and uncertainty stop dependent claims; safe local fixtures and actual command inspection are proportionate. Full historical suites and live publication are not required merely to assess prose cleanup. Final independent whole-change Code Review and distinct Verify remain explicit.

No project-map reliance: the exact source package, displacement map and bounded source/implementation inspection provide the assessment basis. No repository-wide dependency audit or hosted/current release execution is claimed. The two corrections are author-owned and do not require reconsidering approved proposal direction.

## Independence and checks

This is a separate reviewer agent. The parent authored the engineering contribution; this reviewer made no package, proposal, activity or work edits and no commits. Inspected full scoped primary context, all package members, current proposal/r2, six originals and exact architecture excerpts. Read the current release_transaction.py classification/timing definitions only to distinguish supported representation from standing policy; did not treat implementation as a policy supersession. Primary subject inspect supplied every stored identity. review record and finding add help were read before targeted recording. Record-store validation follows saving; it establishes structural persistence only. No runtime, package, live public smoke, publication or historical benchmark command was run.

## Finding design-r1-f1

- Finding ID: design-r1-f1
- Severity: Major
- Location: docs/design/release/release.md — REL-SR-01/03, Context and Scope, routine-profile representation and transaction R1–6 displacement row
- Evidence: The source release-transaction-automation.md Glossary defines the routine automation population explicitly: same package, supported target set, publication channels and evidence schema, no emergency/security exception, no new adapter class, no release-schema migration and no historical-evidence rewrite. R5/R6 and RTA-T002/T019 make that classification enforceable. Release preserves the general standing-process no-new-decision rule and says special releases need an owner, but does not define this narrower automation population completely. In particular an already-authorized emergency/security exception or schema migration is not a new decision at execution time, yet still cannot be classified as routine automation merely because REL-SR-01 is satisfied. The model is removing the only explicit definition while mapping R1–6 as completely transferred.
- Required outcome: Define the retained routine-automation population and its special-release exclusions explicitly in Release, separate from the standing-process routine-publication boundary. Preserve explicit owner handling for special releases without implying that an owner decision makes them routine or that current tools support special execution. Reconcile the mapping and relevant representative outcome. This requires a compact definition, not a new schema, implementation or release gate.
- Safe resolution path: design author makes the bounded retained-contract correction, declares subject/applicability impact and returns the exact package for independent reassessment.
- needs-decision rationale: none.
- Finding scope: artifact-local
- Affected artifact IDs: release
- Owning stages: design

## Finding design-r1-f2

- Finding ID: design-r1-f2
- Severity: Minor
- Location: docs/design/release/release.md — REL-SR-18, Timing representation row and transaction R39–42/RTA-T022 displacement rows
- Evidence: Transaction R42 and RTA-T022 require separate available observations for preflight, local verification, the GitHub release job, npm publish job, public smoke and closeout. Standing release-process flow step 12 repeats that requirement. REL-SR-18 instead names preparation, preflight, local/CI verification, publication waiting and public closeout, including publication/smoke limitations. This does not require separate npm-job and public-smoke observations: a single public_closeout duration plus a limitation note satisfies the new prose even when separate measurements exist. The closed phase enum is a representation constraint, not an adopted supersession of R42; its check rows can carry separate observations. All original definitions are selected for deletion.
- Required outcome: Retain the exact available-operation separation required by R42, including GitHub release job, npm publish job and public smoke, and explain its use of existing phase/check evidence without expanding the closed enum. Keep availability qualification, explicit missing-result limits and advisory duration meaning. If an actual adopted amendment supersedes the distinction, name that disposition instead. No new runtime suite or duration budget is requested.
- Safe resolution path: design author makes the bounded retained-contract correction, declares subject/applicability impact and returns the exact package for independent reassessment.
- needs-decision rationale: none.
- Finding scope: artifact-local
- Affected artifact IDs: release
- Owning stages: design
